author: reek
body: This test runs the driver against the emulated e1000 in the Device Emulation Catalog, so unlike e1000-match it DOES touch registers, both descriptor rings and a frame. Its `.vmargs` selects the model and the fault, if any.

author: reek
body: What a green result here is evidence of, and it is worth being exact: that the driver's own state machine advances and that it survives each refusal the model can produce. The model and the driver were written by the same agent from the same datasheet reading, so a misreading passes both. It is not evidence about silicon, and the hardware sitting stays the referee.

author: reek
body: The received frame is reported byte for byte rather than as a count. A length alone would be satisfied by any sixty bytes, including sixty bytes of uninitialised buffer, and the canned frame carries a broadcast destination with an unassigned EtherType precisely so that its bytes could not have come from anywhere else.
